title: Inventory reconciliation
prompt: Build a CLI reading one JSON object {expected,observed} from stdin; both are CSV texts. CSV rules: UTF-8 text; records end with LF or CRLF; fields may be double-quoted, in which case they may contain commas, line breaks and doubled quotes ("" means one quote); a double quote inside an unquoted field is an ordinary character; a closing quote must be followed by a comma, a line ending or the end of input, otherwise the input is not valid CSV; a leading byte order mark is ignored; completely empty lines are skipped; an unterminated quoted field makes the input invalid. Each header must be exactly sku,qty, otherwise (and for empty CSV texts, invalid CSV or malformed input JSON) exit nonzero, leave stdout empty and write a diagnostic to stderr. A data record is rejected, and counted for its side, when it has other than 2 fields, when after trimming surrounding whitespace sku is empty or qty is not one or more ASCII digits, or when its sku (exact string) was already accepted earlier on the same side (the first accepted record wins). Compare the accepted records by sku; a sku is present on a side even when its qty is 0. additions are skus only observed, removals are skus only expected, changes are skus on both sides with different integer quantities; unchanged skus are omitted. Print exactly one JSON object and a newline: {additions,removals,changes,rejected} where additions and removals are arrays of {sku,qty} (qty an integer), changes is an array of {sku,expected,observed} (integers), each sorted by sku in plain code-unit string order, and rejected is {expected,observed} counts. Exit 0 on success. No external services are needed.
